messages:
anya: Kicking off cerberus-8b int4 quant sweep on staging. Observed OOMs with a pattern: triggers only when concurrent microbatch > 2 and max_new_tokens >= 600. Posting logs and config.

jess: can you paste the exact canary config? quick glance helps.

anya: sure, copying the canary config we used:
```
model: cerberus-8b
precision: int4
batching:
  microbatch: 4
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
max_new_tokens: 768
prefetch: true
kv_trim: auto
```

michael: hmm KV cache will blow up for long sequences. what's the seq-len distribution in the test traffic?

anya: ~85% short queries <=128, but ~2% long ones >1000 (these are the culprits). Pattern: many short requests interleaved with one long -> allocator fragmentation over time.

rachel: can you share repro steps so infra can reproduce on a smaller cluster?

anya: repro script: run 20 short prompts (<=100 tokens) then 1 long prompt (1200 tokens) in a tight loop. Error snippet below when it OOMs:
```
OOM: CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.2GB
runtime/infer.cpp:243
slot_alloc: failed to find contiguous block after multiple frees
```

infra-bot: Auto-suggestion: try kv_trim=aggressive and reduce microbatch to 1 for canary. Also consider disabling prefetch for now.

jess: agree. Also set a conservative max_new_tokens default for canary (256). Soft-throttle maximum concurrency to 2 while we observe.

michael: ran a quick repro locally with microbatch=1, kv_trim=aggressive, prefetch=false — no OOMs. Latency downside: ~20% increase for short queries. So it's a clear tradeoff.

anya: noted. we should measure p50/p95/p99 and token unit cost. I'll set up two routes: cerb-int4-v1 (current) and cerb-int4-v2 (tuned) and run A/B.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: cerb-int4-v2 -> rollout 5% at 2026-03-21T12:30:00Z (canary window 30m). Monitoring hooks enabled.

rachel: also propose batch-pacing heuristic: prefer slightly larger microbatches for truly short bursts but avoid building KV for long sequences. windowed batching maybe.

michael: I can prototype a microbatch heuristic: if estimated_total_tokens < 512 then microbatch=2 else microbatch=1. cheap estimator from token histogram.

anya: plan for canary: kv_trim=aggressive, microbatch heuristic (michael's), max_new_tokens default 256, prefetch=false. collect p50/p95/p99 + per-route token cost and OOM alerts. I'll post numbers here.

jess: if canary still OOMs, fallback route should hit float16 model variant automatically. Add that to the rollout policy.

anya: acknowledged, starting canary.

anya: Canary update after 30m: no OOMs observed. p99 latency increased by ~12% but token cost decreased ~18%. Quick stats (v1 -> v2): p50 42ms -> 48ms, p95 210ms -> 235ms, p99 480ms -> 538ms. Cost per 1K tokens: $1.12 -> $0.92. No error traces in logs.

michael: that looks like an acceptable trade for staging/most customers. Recommend promoting these knobs as default for int4 cerberus-8b.

jess: I'll update the model catalog entry: default max_new_tokens=256, kv_trim=aggressive, prefetch=false, and note 'high fragility for long sequences; use float16 fallback for extremely long seqs'. cc @devex for docs.

rachel: nice work. follow-up: can we explore dynamic prefetch so only sequences >400 tokens enable prefetch? should reduce fragmentation while preserving perf for long requests.

anya: added to follow-up backlog. :party_parrot: closing this thread once docs + rollout PR are merged.
